title: Netflix Unveils Operation Safed Sagar, an IAF Kargil War Series Premiering August 7
excerpt: The military drama stars Siddharth and Jimmy Shergill as Indian Air Force officers who led the world's highest air operation during the 1999 Kargil conflict.
body:
• Netflix has unveiled the trailer for Operation Safed Sagar, a military drama series about the Indian Air Force's role in the 1999 Kargil War, premiering August 7.
  • The series stars Siddharth as Squadron Leader Ajay Ahuja and Jimmy Shergill as Wing Commander B.S. Dhanoa, with Abhay Verma, Dia Mirza, and Prajakta Koli in supporting roles.
  • Directed by Oni Sen and filmed at operational IAF bases with real aircraft, the series is described as Netflix India's most ambitious production to date.
  • Air Chief Marshal (Retd.) B.S. Dhanoa, who led the real operation, served as a consultant and hopes the series will inspire young Indians to join the Air Force.

The Golden Arrows Take Flight

Netflix has released the full trailer for Operation Safed Sagar, a military drama series chronicling the Indian Air Force's high-altitude air campaign during the 1999 Kargil War. The series, which premieres on August 7, follows the Golden Arrows Squadron as it executes some of the most perilous aerial missions in Indian military history — operations recognised as the world's highest air combat engagement.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=vqV3xfeb4SQ

Jimmy Shergill portrays Wing Commander B.S. Dhanoa — later Air Chief Marshal — who led the squadron during the 47-day campaign against Pakistani forces occupying strategic positions across mountain terrain exceeding 16,000 feet. Siddharth plays Squadron Leader Ajay Ahuja, a pilot whose role in the conflict became one of its most significant chapters. The ensemble cast includes Abhay Verma, Dia Mirza, Prajakta Koli, Adil Hussain, Mihir Ahuja, Taaruk Raina, Arnav Bhasin, and Amrita Bagchi.

"If this series succeeds in igniting that spark and encourages more young Indians to join the Indian Air Force, I would consider that my objective achieved."</p><cite>— Air Chief Marshal (Retd.) B.S."

Netflix India's Most Ambitious Production

The series was filmed across operational Indian Air Force bases with access to actual aircraft and military infrastructure, recreating conditions in real high-altitude environments. Monika Shergill, Vice-President of Content at Netflix India, called it the platform's "most ambitious production in India to date."

"It has been the greatest honor of my life to play Squadron Leader Ajay Ahuja. I want to thank the Indian Air Force for giving us the permission to wear these uniforms."

— Siddharth, Actor

Director Oni Sen, known for the thriller series Asur, worked with creators Abhijeet Singh Parmar and Kushal Srivastava. The script was written by Sandeep Jain, Nikhil Ravi, and Barun Kashyap, with production by Matchbox Shots LLP and Feel Good Films.

Guided by the Man Who Led the Mission

Air Chief Marshal (Retd.) B.S. Dhanoa, who commanded the Golden Arrows during the actual operation, served as a consultant on the project. His involvement underscores the authenticity the makers pursued — the production team conducted extensive research and consulted IAF veterans and families connected to the mission.

"India is ready to hear this story now. In fact, it is long overdue. If this series succeeds in igniting that spark and encourages more young Indians to join the Indian Air Force, I would consider that my objective achieved."

— Air Chief Marshal (Retd.) B.S. Dhanoa

Indian Military Stories Go Global

Operation Safed Sagar represents a growing trend of Indian military narratives reaching global audiences through streaming platforms. For the Indian diaspora, the series taps into deep patriotic sentiment around the Kargil War — a conflict that remains a defining national memory for Indians who came of age in the late 1990s. The August 7 premiere coincides closely with Kargil Vijay Diwas, observed annually on July 26, when India commemorates its victory in the conflict.

The series joins a growing slate of Indian-produced content on Netflix that spans beyond Bollywood entertainment into historical and military storytelling, reflecting both India's importance as a subscriber market and the global appetite for stories from the subcontinent.
